commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(`ls /workspace/*/bifrost` finds it). Direct unresolved contract questions to the series lead.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes
and is checked out detached at this exact commit: 2df91bfb592bda73a747d4f56668d616a0c32cb1
Do not fetch from origin or any other remote.
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

History rule. Work only from the base commit above. Do not log, show, diff, check
out or otherwise read any commit, branch or tag that is not an ancestor of the base,
and do not use gh, the GitHub API or the web for this issue, its comments, timeline
or pull requests: the issue text in this brief is complete.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.
If the build cache wrapper stalls, report the evidence to the judge.
Do not bypass the mbx cargo shim, redirect target/, set CARGO_TARGET_DIR,
or change shared cache settings.


Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

# Issue

Issue #3488: Python: ship os.environ.get(...) as a process-input source through the declaration route

Follow-up to #3463 (merge 1cbbac59d). The landed row publishes `os.environ["K"]` and `sys.argv[i]` as keyed-read sources. `os.environ.get("K")` is not shipped: it is a call, not a memory load, so the keyed-read route cannot carry it. It needs a declared `os._Environ.get` member in the process-input declaration surface plus receiver-type flow from the `os.environ` value to that member.

The DataFlowBench template-1 cells do not use `.get`, so the acceptance is unaffected, but real Python code reads the environment through `.get` at least as often as through subscripts. Controls must match the subscript route: a shadowed `os`, a local `environ`, and a reassigned root stay clean by identity, not spelling.

FINAL REPORT

I fixed #3488 with two changes to the Python type flow. `os.environ.get("K")` reaching `os.system` now reports one definite finding on a conclusive run. A shadowed `os`, a local `environ`, and a reassigned root report nothing. All work is committed on the detached HEAD; the working tree is clean.

## 1. Confirmed cause

The test setup was an active model declaring the `os` module field `environ` with type `os._Environ`, plus a declared `get` method on that class. The fixture policy selects `get` with `resolved-call :proof declared` and binds `return-value`. At the base commit, `os.environ.get(...)` reaching `os.system` binds no source (`src=0`), reports nothing, and the run is `inconclusive`. The source selector's diagnostic was `call_bindings did not establish complete actual-to-formal coverage (dispatch outcome=unproven, coverage=open, target_count=1)`.

Two engine gaps were responsible. I confirmed both with temporary debug output, which I removed before committing.

- **Cause 1: the receiver was never typed.** `python_exact_value_class_at_in_query` in `crates/bifrost-python-analysis/src/analyzer/python/type_flow.rs` split the `os.environ` load into its base `os` and an `environ` access. It then stopped at `os`: the trace showed `value kind=Temporary node kind=identifier text="os"`, and a module object has no exact class. The import binder was asked only about local or temporary values, never about a load. So `python_exact_external_receiver_identities` returned `None` and dispatch stayed unproven. `external_module_value_seed`, which reads declared module value types, was already used by the class-set path but not by this exact walk.
- **Cause 2: a lowering claim on the load stayed open.** After fixing cause 1, the run was still inconclusive ("procedure semantics for run is unknown"). The blocking gap was `SemanticGap { subject: Value(6), capability: Calls, kind: Unknown, discharge: RuntimeReadBehavior, detail: "descriptor or special-method invocation requires type refinement" }` on the `os.environ` load. Before this change, only three things could discharge it:
  - the callee value of a resolved call;
  - the reviewed keyed-read model (the subscript route);
  - the #4651 rule for declared fields read through `self`.

  An `os.environ` value used as a receiver is none of these.

The `.get` call also needs a model under `:unmodeled require-model`; the shipped `os.system` closes only through its summary. I supplied a test-only summary for `os._Environ.get`.

Your two notes, both now tested:
- At base, `os.environ.get` is not a source: confirmed (`src=0`).
- A `.get` call refutes subscript reads in the same module: confirmed. With the shipped #3463 policy, a file with only `os.environ["K"]` reaching `os.system` gives `proven_by_summary` with 1 finding. Adding `return os.environ.get("OTHER")` in another function gives `inconclusive` with 0 findings. This is the same before and after my change.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Base: `2df91bfb592bda73a747d4f56668d616a0c32cb1`. Commits: `9a483f4bcbcdc1b2e8da8f4ff235f5724085b0ff` (fix and tests) and `b9c425d3e8bb88e6b7e211aa76c98f038acd5952` (final: design note and test formatting).

- **`type_flow.rs`, exact receiver walk.** A load is now first checked with the import binder. If the binder binds it to a module field that an active model declares with `value_type`, that declared class is the receiver's origin. Because Python code can replace a module attribute, this exact claim also needs the existing workspace scan for member writes and module-object escapes (`python_workspace_module_member_mutation_free`, cached per member). Otherwise the receiver is unknown.
- **`type_flow.rs`, field-read gap discharge.** `python_external_field_read_discharges_gap` now also discharges the descriptor claim in one case: the binder binds the access to a module, and the model declares the member as one static field of that module. A module is not a class instance, so no descriptor runs, and a field that is present never reaches a module `__getattr__`. The binder already refuses a shado

d. Two gaps in the Python type flow blocked it. First, the exact receiver walk split the `os.environ` read into the `os` module and an access, and a module has no class to start from. It now asks the import binder about the whole read and uses the field's declared type. Because code can replace a module attribute, that claim also needs proof that no workspace file writes `os.environ` or passes the `os` module around. Second, Python lowering marks every attribute read as one that might run a descriptor. For a module field that the binder proves and the model declares, that cannot happen, so the read now closes that claim. A shadowed `os`, a local `environ`, and a reassigned root never reach the declared member, because the binder refuses them by identity. The regression test runs `bifrost scan` with test-only declaration, summary, and policy fixtures, since the product packs are frozen. Before the change, every positive was inconclusive with no finding; after it, template 1 with `.get` reports one definite finding on a conclusive run. The DataFlowBench template-1 cells give the same results before and after. Two follow-ups remain: `from os import environ` is not yet an exact receiver, and any method call on `os.environ` still makes subscript reads in the same module incomplete.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- In Bifrost, getting a source to bind is only half the work. The finding was `definite` once cause 1 was fixed, but the run stayed `inconclusive` because an unrelated lowering claim on the same load was still open. Run completeness and finding certainty are tracked separately.
- The import binder carries the identity checks (shadowing, uniqueness, reassignment). Reusing it in both the receiver walk and the gap discharge excludes the controls without any name matching.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
